correctness.rationale: For every integer \(m\ge1\), the same-spin edge count \(E=(3m^2+s_As_B+s_As_C+s_Bs_C)/2\) is minimized exactly by two opposite monochromatic parts. Successively purifying the three parts toward the sign opposite the sum of the remaining magnetizations gives a valid non-increasing path to those minimizers. Ground states are reversible and joined by six monochromatic junctions, yielding one irreducible aperiodic class of \(6(2^m-1)\) states and uniform stationarity. Boundary-edge counting gives \(\Phi=2/[3(2^m-2)]\) and a union-bound proof of \(t_{\mathrm{mix}}(1/4)\ge2^{m-1}\). Kac’s identity gives junction mean return time \(2^m-1\). The standalone checker exhaustively verified \(1\le m\le5\), from \(8\) to \(32768\) configurations, without replacing the infinite-family proof.

value.rationale: The original stochastic minority literature explicitly emphasizes topology-dependent recurrence/convergence, yet nonbipartite cases are less tractable. On the natural complete tripartite octahedral blow-ups, the result identifies all recurrent configurations and the full invariant distribution for every m, and proves an exponential equilibrium bottleneck caused by six rare junctions. This is structurally motivated dynamical content, not an arbitrary numerical slice or known-table recomputation.
